Macroeconomics aims to explain and predict recessions and recovery patterns.
Economics as a whole studies decisions under limited resources at micro and macro levels.
Microeconomics cannot study unemployment because unemployment exists only at macro level.
tactical_explanations:
National GDP falling for two quarters and job losses across the economy are whole-economy aggregates. Those are macroeconomic phenomena.

So the statement is True.

A single shop closing and dismissing two workers is a firm-level layoff. Sharing a word with the recession headline does not promote that shop into macro analysis. Macro here is the economy-wide GDP drop and job-loss totals, not one employer’s roster change.

So the statement is False.

Explaining why output and employment fall together, and forecasting how recoveries unfold, is core macro work. Recession and recovery patterns are exactly the kind of economy-wide dynamics the field targets.

So the statement is True.

Economics as a discipline covers scarce-resource decisions at every scale. Micro takes households, firms, and particular markets; macro takes national income, employment, and the price level. The recession headline sits on the macro side, yet the same scarcity foundation still underwrites both branches. Limited resources force choices whether the unit is one shop or the whole labour force.

So the statement is True.

Micro can study a worker’s job search or one firm’s hiring even though national unemployment is a macro aggregate. Existence of a macro series does not ban micro questions about unemployment.

So the statement is False.

title: Freonia quarterly report
context: Consider freonia's statistics office reports national growth, unemployment, and central-bank interest rates each quarter. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: This whole-economy report is macroeconomic analysis rather than a single unit's decision.
Growth, unemployment, and interest rates are macroeconomic topics alongside inflation and price levels.
One bakery studying only its own sales and staffing would be microeconomics.
Economics as a science builds theories to explain and predict such nationwide phenomena.
Both branches fall under economics defined as decisions under limited resources.
tactical_explanations:
Freonia’s quarterly pack of national growth, unemployment, and policy rates summarises the whole economy, not one firm’s decision. That is macroeconomic analysis.

So the statement is True.

Growth, unemployment, and central-bank interest rates belong with inflation and the price level on the macro list. Freonia’s statistics office is publishing exactly those economy-wide variables each quarter.

So the statement is True.

A bakery watching only its own sales and staffing is studying one firm. That unit of analysis is microeconomics.

So the statement is True.

As a science, economics builds theories that explain nationwide movements and that support predictions about them. Freonia’s growth and unemployment releases are the kind of phenomena those theories address.

So the statement is True.

Micro and macro are branches of one subject. Both start from decisions under limited resources; they part ways on whether the question tracks a single unit or economy-wide totals. Freonia’s national report and a bakery’s staffing plan therefore sit under the same economics umbrella at different scopes.

So the statement is True.

title: Household heating bill
context: Consider the Weiss family compares gas versus heat-pump suppliers for next winter's contract, ignoring national energy policy. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Macroeconomics cannot explain recessions because only micro markets exist.
Energy is always macroeconomics because heating affects national consumption statistics.
If policymakers analysed total household energy use affecting national inflation, that would be macroeconomics.
Economics studies such household trade-offs under a limited monthly budget.
Micro and macro ask identical questions, so analysing the Weiss family equals analysing the nation.
tactical_explanations:
Macroeconomics exists precisely to explain recessions and other whole-economy swings. The claim that only micro markets exist, so macro cannot speak to downturns, denies that second scope. The Weiss family’s heating contract is a micro choice; recession analysis is a different, aggregate question.

So the statement is False.

Energy is not locked into macro because heating shows up in national consumption data. The Weiss family’s supplier comparison, with national policy set aside, remains a household micro decision.

So the statement is False.

Shift the object to total household energy use and its imprint on national inflation, and the same sector becomes a macro problem. Policymakers reading economy-wide energy demand for inflation are doing macroeconomics.

So the statement is True.

Choosing gas versus a heat pump under a limited monthly budget is a classic scarce-resource household trade-off. Economics studies exactly those choices.

So the statement is True.

Micro and macro do not ask identical questions. Studying the Weiss family’s winter contract is not the same exercise as studying the nation’s energy use or inflation. One tracks a single household’s alternatives; the other tracks aggregates. Equating the two collapses the scope distinction the chapter uses.

So the statement is False.

title: Export statistics release
context: Consider the trade ministry publishes total national exports and imports for the year. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Whole-country export and import totals are macroeconomic statistics.
One exporting winery's shipment schedule to Germany is macroeconomics because trade crosses a border.
Macro topics include growth, unemployment, inflation, and interest rates alongside aggregates like trade totals.
Economics tries to explain why national export performance changes over time.
Microeconomics studies individual firms' export decisions when those firms are the unit analysed.
tactical_explanations:
Country-wide export and import totals are aggregates for the whole economy. Those trade figures are macroeconomic statistics.

So the statement is True.

One winery’s shipment calendar to Germany is a single firm’s logistics plan. Crossing a border does not by itself turn that plan into macro analysis. Macro appears when the ministry’s national export and import totals are the object, not when one exporter books a truck.

So the statement is False.

Macro’s usual cast includes growth, unemployment, inflation, and interest rates. National trade totals sit beside those aggregates as another economy-wide measure.

So the statement is True.

Economics aims to explain movements such as why a country’s export performance rises or falls over time. Theories link exchange rates, demand abroad, costs at home, and related forces to those national outcomes. The ministry’s annual trade release is raw material for that explanatory work.

So the statement is True.

When the unit analysed is one firm’s export decision, the question is microeconomic even though trade also appears in national accounts.

So the statement is True.

title: Confusing scope with topic
context: Consider students debate whether 'prices' and 'jobs' are always macro or micro topics. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Micro and macro study identical questions with no meaningful difference in scope.
Any discussion of wages is automatically macroeconomics because labour markets are national.
Economy-wide average wage growth published by a statistics office is macroeconomics.
A household choosing between two job offers compares micro-level alternatives under limited time.
Economics cannot explain individual choices, only nationwide aggregates.
tactical_explanations:
Micro and macro differ in scope: individual units and particular markets versus economy-wide aggregates. They do not study identical questions.

So the statement is False.

Wages are not automatically macro. A firm setting one worker’s pay or a household weighing two offers is still micro, even though labour markets can also be measured nationally. Topic words such as “wages” or “jobs” do not freeze the label; the scope of the question does.

So the statement is False.

An economy-wide average wage-growth number from a statistics office is an aggregate. That publication is macroeconomics.

So the statement is True.

A household picking between two job offers under limited time is comparing personal alternatives. That is a micro-level choice, not a reading of national labour aggregates.

So the statement is True.

Economics is not confined to nationwide aggregates. Microeconomics exists to explain individual choices — which job to take, what to buy, how a firm prices — under scarcity. Saying the subject can only speak to economy-wide totals erases the household and firm half of the field the students are debating.

So the statement is False.

title: Teacher's scope quiz
context: Consider a teacher lists examples and asks which are micro versus macro. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Micro examines individual households, businesses, or markets; macro examines the whole economy.
A single consumer choosing organic milk is microeconomics.
National unemployment rate is macroeconomics.
Economics explains and predicts at both scopes using theories about limited resources.
If an example mentions government, it must always be classified as macroeconomics.
tactical_explanations:
The classroom split is standard: micro looks at individual households, businesses, or markets; macro looks at the economy as a whole. That is the sorting rule the teacher’s quiz is testing.

So the statement is True.

Organic milk on one shopping trip is a single consumer choosing among grocery options. That household purchase sits in microeconomics, not in national aggregates.

So the statement is True.

The national unemployment rate summarises the whole labour market. It is a macroeconomic indicator.

So the statement is True.

At both scopes, economics uses theories about limited resources to explain behaviour and to predict outcomes. Micro and macro differ in the unit studied, not in whether theory and prediction apply.

So the statement is True.

Mentioning government does not force a macro label. A household applying for one means-tested benefit, or a firm bidding on one public contract, can still be micro if that single unit is the object of study. Macro needs an economy-wide question — national spending, the price level, aggregate employment — not merely the word “government” in the stem.

So the statement is False.

title: BrewPeak espresso price hike
context: Consider inês raises BrewPeak espresso prices after imported bean costs rise, thinking only about her Porto shop. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: National unemployment figures belong to microeconomics because each worker is an individual.
Macroeconomics is simply the study of any price change, including one café's espresso price.
Microeconomics never studies how two firms interact in one product market.
Macroeconomics refuses to discuss inflation because inflation starts in single shops.
Economics remains a science building theories to explain and predict behaviour despite imperfect human prediction.
tactical_explanations:
National unemployment figures are aggregates even though each unemployed person is an individual. Counting the whole labour force’s joblessness is macro work, not micro because the raw units are people. Inês raising BrewPeak’s espresso price remains the micro contrast in this case.

So the statement is False.

Macroeconomics is not “any price change.” One café’s espresso hike is a firm-level price decision; macro tracks economy-wide price levels and related aggregates.

So the statement is False.

Microeconomics routinely studies how firms interact in one product market — rivalry, pricing responses, differentiation. Saying it never does that erases a large part of industrial organisation and market analysis. BrewPeak reacting to bean costs is exactly the kind of firm behaviour micro examines, including against nearby cafés.

So the statement is False.

Inflation is a central macro topic: the rise in the overall price level. Single-shop price changes can feed into that aggregate, but they do not make macro “refuse” to discuss inflation. Inês’s Porto menu is micro; Freonia-style CPI or euro-area inflation readings are macro. Both price stories can appear in economics without one cancelling the other.

So the statement is False.

Economics still builds theories to explain and predict behaviour even though people forecast imperfectly. Imperfect prediction does not strip the subject of its scientific aims.

So the statement is True.

title: Micro scope traps
context: Analyze traps students face when classifying examples as microeconomic rather than macroeconomic. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A single farmer choosing between wheat and vegetable crops on limited irrigation water is microeconomics.
A single bakery setting its loaf price after flour costs rise is microeconomics.
A city bus company setting a new single-route fare is microeconomics when only that firm's pricing is analysed.
National GDP growth rate publication is macroeconomics because it summarises the entire economy.
Microeconomics can explain and predict behaviour of individual markets, households, and firms.
tactical_explanations:
One farmer allocating scarce irrigation between wheat and vegetables is a single producer’s choice. That is microeconomics.

So the statement is True.

A bakery resetting its loaf price after flour costs rise is one firm adjusting in its product market. The unit of analysis stays micro even though flour prices may also move in national data.

So the statement is True.

When only the bus company’s own route fare is under study, the question is firm-level pricing. That keeps the example in microeconomics despite the public-service setting.

So the statement is True.

Published GDP growth for the whole country compresses every sector into one output figure. Because the summary covers the entire economy, the publication is macroeconomics.

So the statement is True.

Microeconomics’ job is to explain and predict how individual markets, households, and firms behave under scarcity. Crop mix, loaf pricing, and a single-route fare are all inside that remit. The trap to avoid is treating every familiar topic word as macro; scope of the unit analysed still decides the label.

So the statement is True.

title: Ride-hail surge pricing
context: Consider one ride-hail platform raises fares in one city district after a concert ends. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Studying surge pricing for one platform in one district is microeconomics.
Surge pricing is macroeconomics because many riders are affected at once.
If analysts measured whether district fare spikes raised the city's overall consumer price index, that index move would be macroeconomics.
Economics can predict how riders and drivers respond to a local price spike.
Individual market pricing never falls within economics because only governments set prices.
tactical_explanations:
Surge pricing for one platform in one district is a local market pricing problem. Studying that response is microeconomics.

So the statement is True.

Many riders feeling the same concert-night spike does not make the episode macro. The object is still one platform’s fares in one district, not the economy’s overall price level or output. Crowd size inside a local market is not the same as an economy-wide aggregate.

So the statement is False.

If analysts ask whether those district spikes moved the city’s overall consumer price index, the object becomes an aggregate price measure. That index movement is read as macroeconomics.

So the statement is True.

Economics can predict how riders cut trips or how drivers reposition when a local fare spikes. Those responses are exactly the kind of behaviour theory targets.

So the statement is True.

Individual market pricing sits squarely inside economics — especially microeconomics. Governments are not the only price setters; platforms, shops, and other private sellers set prices constantly. The concert-night surge is a private pricing rule under local scarcity of rides, and it is a legitimate economic object of study.

So the statement is False.

title: Competition authority case
context: Consider regulators investigate whether three mobile carriers colluded on text-message pricing nationally. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Investigating pricing across an entire national mobile market can involve macro-style market-wide analysis.
One subscriber choosing a cheaper text plan for her own phone is microeconomics.
Economics builds theories to explain firm behaviour and market outcomes including competition issues.
Microeconomics studies individual firm pricing strategies when one carrier alone is analysed.
Economics excludes market competition because only government budgets matter.
tactical_explanations:
Looking at text-message pricing across the whole national mobile market widens the lens beyond one carrier’s private spreadsheet. Market-wide collusion questions can draw on that broader, aggregate-style reading of the industry.

So the statement is True.

The statement points at one subscriber’s plan choice. In this case the live question is national pricing among three carriers, not that private handset decision, so the letter does not correctly describe the analysis under study.

So the statement is False.

Economics builds theories of firm behaviour and market outcomes, including how rivalry or collusion shapes prices. Competition-authority questions sit inside that explanatory project.

So the statement is True.

When analysts isolate one carrier’s pricing strategy alone, the unit is a single firm. That is microeconomics.

So the statement is True.

Market competition is a central economic topic, especially in micro and industrial organisation. Government budgets matter in public finance, but they do not monopolise the subject or push rivalry off the syllabus. The carriers’ alleged text-price collusion is precisely the sort of market-outcome question economics studies.

So the statement is False.

title: Bookstore pricing experiment
context: Consider a regional bookstore chain tests a 5% price cut in one city branch and tracks only that branch's weekly revenue. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Analysing one branch's revenue after its own price change is microeconomics.
Central bank inflation targeting for an entire currency area is macroeconomics.
If the national statistics office later reported economy-wide consumer price inflation, that would be macroeconomics.
Micro focuses on individual households, businesses, and markets rather than the whole economy.
Economics tries to explain and predict outcomes such as how a branch responds to a price cut.
tactical_explanations:
Tracking one branch’s weekly revenue after its own 5% cut is firm-unit analysis. That is microeconomics.

So the statement is True.

Inflation targeting by a central bank for an entire currency area is an economy-wide policy problem. That belongs to macroeconomics, not to the bookstore’s branch experiment.

So the statement is True.

Economy-wide consumer price inflation reported by the national statistics office is an aggregate. That release is macroeconomics.

So the statement is True.

Microeconomics stays with individual households, businesses, and markets. It does not take the whole economy’s totals as its primary object — that is macro’s job.

So the statement is True.

Economics tries to explain and predict outcomes such as how a branch’s revenue moves after a price cut. Demand responses, rival stores, and margin effects are the kind of behaviour theory is built to handle at the micro scope. The chain’s one-city experiment is a concrete instance of that predictive aim.

So the statement is True.

title: Kelvinia rate rise
context: Consider kelvinia's central bank raises the key interest rate nationwide to slow inflation. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: GDP growth and one household's grocery list are analysed with identical tools and the same scope.
Interest rates on national policy are a micro topic because each loan is signed by one borrower.
Microeconomics covers only diagrams; macroeconomics covers only newspaper opinion.
Because mortgages of specific families change, the central-bank move is automatically microeconomics.
Economics tries to build theories explaining why central banks raise rates and predict inflation effects.
tactical_explanations:
GDP growth is an economy-wide aggregate; a household grocery list is a single unit’s consumption plan. They are not analysed with identical tools or the same scope. Kelvinia’s rate rise is a national policy move aimed at inflation — a macro setting that does not collapse into one family’s shopping list.

So the statement is False.

A nationwide policy rate is a macro instrument even though each mortgage is signed by one borrower. The policy object is the whole economy’s borrowing conditions and inflation, not one loan file.

So the statement is False.

Neither branch is a cartoon of “only diagrams” versus “only newspaper opinion.” Both use theory, data, and models; they differ by whether the question is unit-level or economy-wide.

So the statement is False.

Mortgage payments of particular families may change after the rate rise, but that side-effect does not reclassify the central-bank decision as microeconomics. The bank’s move is a nationwide inflation tool. A family refinancing its own loan would be a micro story; Kelvinia’s key-rate decision is not that story.

So the statement is False.

Economics builds theories for why central banks raise rates and for how inflation then responds. Explanation and prediction at that aggregate level are part of the subject’s aim.

So the statement is True.

title: Household savings rate national data
context: Consider central bank publishes average household savings rate across the entire country. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Average national household savings rate is a macroeconomic aggregate.
One family increasing its monthly savings by fifty euros is macroeconomics because saving is national policy topic.
Macro includes growth, unemployment, inflation, interest rates, and such economy-wide averages.
Economics explains and predicts how aggregate saving responds to interest rate changes.
Microeconomics studies one family's saving choice when that family alone is the unit analysed.
tactical_explanations:
An average household savings rate for the entire country is an economy-wide aggregate. That figure is macroeconomic.

So the statement is True.

One family raising monthly saving by fifty euros is a single household’s budget change. Calling saving a “national policy topic” in the abstract does not turn that family’s ledger into macro analysis. Macro is the published national average; micro is this one household’s fifty-euro shift.

So the statement is False.

Macro’s usual variables include growth, unemployment, inflation, and interest rates. Economy-wide averages such as the national savings rate sit in that same aggregate family.

So the statement is True.

Linking the national savings average to interest-rate moves is an aggregate prediction problem. Economics builds that kind of macro explanation routinely.

So the statement is True.

When the unit analysed is one family’s saving choice alone, the question is microeconomic. The same word “saving” appears in the central bank’s national average, but the object of study — one household versus the countrywide mean — decides the label.

So the statement is True.

title: Startup funding round
context: Consider ten startups in a city receive venture funding; an analyst studies only one robotics firm's hiring plan. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Choosing a smartphone brand is classified as macroeconomics once the price exceeds €500.
Because venture capital is a national phenomenon, any firm-level study becomes macroeconomics.
Summing all startup investment in the country to assess economic growth would be macroeconomics.
Microeconomics explains and predicts behaviour of individual businesses and markets.
Economics excludes entrepreneurial firms because they are too small for scientific study.
tactical_explanations:
A smartphone brand choice stays a household consumption decision whether the handset costs €200 or €800. Crossing €500 does not promote it into macroeconomics.

So the statement is False.

Venture capital may be discussed as a national trend, but studying one robotics firm’s hiring plan keeps the unit at firm level. A national backdrop does not automatically relabel every firm study as macro.

So the statement is False.

Summing startup investment across the country to judge growth turns the lens to an aggregate. That summation is macroeconomics.

So the statement is True.

Microeconomics explains and predicts how individual businesses and markets behave — including one startup’s hiring under a funding round. That is the branch’s ordinary remit.

So the statement is True.

Entrepreneurial firms are not too small for economic science. Micro theory regularly covers startups’ hiring, pricing, and investment under scarce cash and talent. Excluding them because they are small would erase a large share of real business decisions the field studies.

So the statement is False.

title: Budget airline seat sale
context: Consider a budget airline cuts base fares on one holiday route and tracks bookings for that route only. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Route-level fare and booking analysis for one airline is microeconomics.
Any airfare change is macroeconomics because airlines operate internationally.
Economics predicts how passengers on that route respond to the fare cut under limited budgets.
If the statistics office later reported national transport inflation, that would be macroeconomics.
Household holiday booking under a fare sale is micro consumption choice.
tactical_explanations:
Fare and booking analysis for one airline on one holiday route is firm-and-market micro work.

So the statement is True.

International route maps do not make every airfare change macro. The airline here is tracking bookings on a single route after its own base-fare cut — still a micro pricing experiment.

So the statement is False.

Economics predicts how passengers on that route respond to cheaper seats when their holiday budgets are limited. Quantity responses to a fare cut are a standard demand prediction.

So the statement is True.

National transport inflation from the statistics office is an economy-wide price aggregate. That report is macroeconomics.

So the statement is True.

A household booking a holiday under the fare sale is choosing among scarce travel options and limited income. That consumption choice is microeconomics, parallel to the airline’s route-level experiment on the supply side.

So the statement is True.

title: Elif's weekly work hours
context: Consider elif decides how many bookstore hours cover tuition, rent, and study time without analysing the national job market. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Microeconomics and macroeconomics are unrelated subjects with no shared foundation.
Because Elif is a student not a company, her situation falls outside economics entirely.
Recessions cannot be studied because economics only ever looks at one market at a time.
Economics studies households deciding what to do with limited resources such as time and income.
Without a government bonus, Elif's decision cannot be analysed using economic theory.
tactical_explanations:
Micro and macro are related branches of the same subject. Both rest on scarce-resource decisions; they differ in whether the unit is Elif’s hours or national employment and output. Calling them unrelated subjects with no shared foundation is wrong.

So the statement is False.

Students and other households are core micro actors. Elif allocating bookstore hours among tuition, rent, and study is inside economics, not outside it for lack of a company charter.

So the statement is False.

Economics does not only ever look at one market. Macroeconomics studies recessions as economy-wide contractions of output and employment. Elif’s personal hour choice is micro; that does not ban recession analysis at the aggregate level.

So the statement is False.

Households deciding how to use limited time and income are a central object of economic study. Elif’s weekly hour plan is exactly that kind of decision.

So the statement is True.

No government bonus is required before economic theory can speak. Scarcity of time and income alone is enough to analyse Elif’s trade-off among work, rent, tuition, and study. Policy programmes can change constraints, but their absence does not eject a household decision from economics.

So the statement is False.

title: Green subsidy household
context: Consider a household buys solar panels after a national subsidy lowers the net price; analysts study only this family's payback calculation. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: One family's payback calculation for its own panels is microeconomics.
Because a national subsidy exists, the family's purchase cannot be microeconomics.
Measuring how the subsidy shifted total national renewable investment would be macroeconomics.
Economics studies household investment choices under limited budgets and expected savings.
Policy programmes eliminate the need for microeconomic analysis of individual buyers.
tactical_explanations:
One family’s payback calculation for its own solar panels is a household investment decision. That is microeconomics.

So the statement is True.

A national subsidy can change the net price and still leave the analysis micro if the object is this family’s payback alone. Programme scale in the background does not forbid a household-level reading.

So the statement is False.

Measuring how the subsidy shifted total national renewable investment turns the question into an aggregate. That measurement is macroeconomics.

So the statement is True.

Economics studies household investment choices when budgets are limited and expected energy savings matter. The solar payback arithmetic is a concrete instance of that.

So the statement is True.

Policy programmes do not retire microeconomics. Individual buyers still compare net prices, credit, and payback even when a subsidy is on offer. Analysts studying only this family’s calculation are doing the micro work that remains necessary beside any national programme evaluation.

So the statement is False.

title: National jobs report
context: Consider a labour agency publishes economy-wide job creation and unemployment figures for the past year. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Economy-wide employment totals and unemployment rates are macroeconomic indicators.
Growth, unemployment, inflation, and interest rates are typical macroeconomic variables.
One restaurant deciding whether to extend opening hours is microeconomics when only that firm is studied.
Macro analysis can help explain why unemployment rises during a downturn.
Economics at macro level still concerns decisions and outcomes under limited economy-wide resources.
tactical_explanations:
Economy-wide job creation totals and unemployment rates are macroeconomic indicators.

So the statement is True.

Growth, unemployment, inflation, and interest rates are the usual headline macro variables. The labour agency’s year-end jobs report sits in that same aggregate family.

So the statement is True.

One restaurant weighing longer opening hours, studied alone, is a firm-level decision. That is microeconomics.

So the statement is True.

Macro analysis links downturns to rising unemployment through weaker aggregate demand and related mechanisms. Explaining why joblessness climbs in a recession is part of that work.

So the statement is True.

Even at the macro level, economics still concerns decisions and outcomes under limited resources — labour, capital, and productive capacity for the economy as a whole. The national jobs report is an aggregate lens on those scarce-resource outcomes, not a departure from the scarcity foundation.

So the statement is True.

title: ECB inflation target discussion
context: Consider commentators discuss whether euro-area inflation at 2.3% requires tighter policy across the whole currency bloc. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: If a statement mentions price, it must be macroeconomics regardless of whose price it is.
Inflation measurement for one grocery item in one shop is macroeconomics because inflation is involved.
A household reacting to higher bread prices by switching brands is microeconomics.
Macroeconomics tries to explain and predict economy-wide price level changes and policy responses.
Economics studies only macro aggregates and ignores individual household adjustments entirely.
tactical_explanations:
The word “price” does not force a macro label. Whose price, and whether the object is one item or the economy-wide price level, decides the scope.

So the statement is False.

Tracking one grocery item in one shop is a micro price observation. Invoking the word “inflation” does not convert that shelf tag into macro measurement of the overall price level. Euro-area inflation at 2.3% is the macro object in this case; one shop’s loaf is not.

So the statement is False.

A household switching bread brands after a price rise is a single consumer’s adjustment. That is microeconomics.

So the statement is True.

Macroeconomics explains and predicts movements in the economy-wide price level and the policy responses that follow. Commentators debating tighter euro-area policy at 2.3% inflation are in that lane.

So the statement is True.

Economics does not study only macro aggregates. Microeconomics covers household adjustments such as brand switching when bread gets dearer. Ignoring individual responses would leave out half the subject the ECB discussion sits beside.

So the statement is False.

title: Science of economics
context: Review the scientific aims of economics in explaining and predicting observed phenomena. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Economics builds theories to explain observed economic behaviour and outcomes.
Economics also uses theories to predict likely effects of choices and policies.
Reporting total national car sales after a subsidy programme is macroeconomic analysis.
Both micro and macro contribute explanatory and predictive theory at their respective scopes.
Limited resources forcing choices is the common foundation micro and macro share.
tactical_explanations:
Building theories that explain observed economic behaviour and outcomes is a core scientific aim of economics.

So the statement is True.

The same theories are used to predict likely effects of choices and policies — not only to narrate what already happened. Prediction sits beside explanation in the subject’s aims.

So the statement is True.

Total national car sales after a subsidy are an aggregate series. Reporting them is macroeconomic analysis.

So the statement is True.

Micro and macro each supply explanatory and predictive theory at their own scope. One handles units and particular markets; the other handles economy-wide totals.

So the statement is True.

Limited resources that force choices are the shared foundation under both branches. Whether the decision is one buyer’s car or national sales after a subsidy, scarcity is what makes the economic question arise.

So the statement is True.

title: Town housing permit
context: Consider a municipality approves one apartment block's building permit while ignoring national construction statistics. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Theories cannot guide economics because every person behaves randomly forever.
All construction is macroeconomics because building affects national GDP automatically.
If analysts measured total national housing starts affecting growth, that would be macroeconomics.
Economics can study how limited land and budgets shape one municipality's permit choice.
Households searching for flats never appear in microeconomics because housing is macro only.
tactical_explanations:
Economics uses theories precisely because behaviour is not treated as pure permanent randomness. Patterns in choices under scarcity are what models try to explain and predict. A town’s permit decision for one apartment block is still open to that theoretical reading.

So the statement is False.

Not all construction is macro. One municipality approving a single apartment block, while ignoring national construction statistics, is a local project decision — micro in scope.

So the statement is False.

Total national housing starts tied to growth are an aggregate. Measuring that series for its growth effects is macroeconomics.

So the statement is True.

Limited land and budgets shaping one municipality’s permit choice are scarce-resource decisions economics can study at that local unit.

So the statement is True.

Households searching for flats are a standard micro topic — matching, rents, and search under limited budgets. Housing also appears in macro aggregates, but that does not exile household search from microeconomics. “Housing is macro only” is the trap; scope of the question still decides the label.

So the statement is False.
